more: How Base64 works

Every three bytes of input (24 bits) are split into four groups of six bits, and each group is mapped to one of 64 characters: A–Z, a–z, 0–9, + and /. When the input is not a multiple of three bytes, = signs pad the end. Because text is converted to UTF-8 bytes first, “é” becomes two bytes and “👍” four, which is why short non-English strings can produce longer Base64.
Common pitfalls

Many simple tools use the browser's btoa function directly, which fails on any character outside Latin-1. This encoder converts text to UTF-8 first, matching how servers and most programming languages behave. If decoded text looks garbled, the original data was probably binary (an image or a zip) or used a different character set, such as Windows-1252 or Shift_JIS.

more: v4 or v7?

Version 4 UUIDs are completely random, which is ideal when you do not want identifiers to reveal anything. Version 7, standardised in RFC 9562 in 2024, starts with a 48-bit Unix timestamp in milliseconds followed by random bits. Records created later get larger IDs, so B-tree indexes in PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server stay compact, and you can roughly tell when a record was created.
Format variations

The canonical form is 32 lowercase hexadecimal digits in groups of 8-4-4-4-12. Some systems want them without hyphens (32 characters), in uppercase, or wrapped in braces. The nil UUID, all zeros, is used as a placeholder for “no value”.

more: What each minifier does

The CSS minifier removes comments and whitespace, drops the last semicolon in each block and shortens colours such as #ffffff to #fff. The HTML minifier collapses whitespace between tags and removes comments, while leaving pre, textarea, script and style blocks untouched unless you choose to minify inline code. JavaScript is parsed into a syntax tree by Terser, compressed and printed without comments.
Minification and Core Web Vitals

Smaller files load and parse faster, which helps Largest Contentful Paint and Interaction to Next Paint, two of Google's Core Web Vitals. For large sites, a build tool such as Vite or esbuild is the best long-term option; for small sites, landing pages and quick fixes, this minifier gets you most of the benefit in seconds.

more: Colour models in brief

RGB mixes red, green and blue light and is how screens work. HEX is simply RGB written in hexadecimal. HSL and HSV describe colour by hue (0–360°), saturation and lightness or brightness, which is more intuitive for adjusting colours. CMYK describes cyan, magenta, yellow and black inks for print. Conversions between RGB-based models are exact; CMYK is an approximation without a colour profile.
Accessible colour choices

Around 1 in 12 men and 1 in 200 women have some form of colour vision deficiency, and many people read screens in bright sunlight. Good contrast helps everyone. The contrast ratios here follow the WCAG formula based on relative luminance, the same method used by Lighthouse and accessibility checkers, and they are required by laws and standards such as the European Accessibility Act and the ADA.

more: Percent vs percentage points

If an interest rate rises from 4% to 5%, it has gone up by 1 percentage point – but by 25% in relative terms. News reports and financial statements mix these up surprisingly often. The calculator shows both, so you can quote figures correctly in reports, presentations and articles.
Mental shortcuts

10% of any number moves the decimal point one place left; 5% is half of that; 1% moves it two places. So 15% of 80 is 8 + 4 = 12. Also, X% of Y always equals Y% of X: 8% of 50 is the same as 50% of 8, which is 4. These tricks help you check that the calculator's answer is in the right ballpark.

more: How age is calculated

The calculator counts full years first, then full months, then remaining days, borrowing days from the previous month when needed – the same method used on official forms. For example, from 31 January to 1 March is 1 month and 1 day in a non-leap year. Totals such as days and weeks are exact counts of calendar days between the two dates.
Age conventions around the world

Most countries use the international age system shown here, where you are 0 at birth and gain a year on each birthday. South Korea officially switched to this system in 2023, replacing its traditional counting; parts of East Asia still use traditional reckoning informally. When forms ask for age, use the international system unless told otherwise.

more: The formula

BMI equals weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared. For imperial units, the calculator converts pounds to kilograms (× 0.4536) and inches to centimetres (× 2.54) first. For example, 70 kg and 1.75 m gives 70 ÷ (1.75 × 1.75) = 22.9. BMI Prime is your BMI divided by the upper limit of the normal range, so values above 1.0 indicate overweight.
Asian cut-off points

A WHO expert consultation found that people of Asian descent often have higher health risks at lower BMI values. Many countries in Asia therefore use 23 as the threshold for overweight and 27.5 for higher risk. Tick the option to apply these cut-offs. The calculator gives information only and is not medical advice; your data never leaves your device.

more: The amortisation formula

The regular payment is P × r ÷ (1 − (1 + r)^−n), where P is the amount borrowed, r is the interest rate per period and n is the number of payments. Early payments are mostly interest because the balance is high; over time, more of each payment goes towards the principal. The year-by-year table makes this shift easy to see.
Mortgages in different countries

Loan structures vary. Thirty-year fixed mortgages are common in the United States, while the UK, Canada and Australia typically fix the rate for 2–5 years within a 25–30-year term, and many European and Asian loans use variable rates. Use the current rate for the whole term to estimate payments, then rerun the numbers with a higher rate to test whether you could afford a rise.

more: Stacked discounts explained

When a store offers an extra discount on sale items, each discount applies to the result of the previous one. 40% off followed by an extra 20% off means you pay 60% × 80% = 48% of the original price, a 52% discount rather than 60%. The calculator shows this effective discount so there are no surprises at the till.
Tax added or included

Prices in North America usually exclude sales tax, which varies by state, province or city. Most other countries show prices including VAT or GST, often 5–27%. Choose “already included” to see how much of the price is tax – useful for business expense claims and VAT refunds for tourists.

more: Working days around the world

Most of the world uses a Saturday–Sunday weekend, but some countries in the Middle East use Friday–Saturday, others have a Friday-only or Sunday-only weekend, and many businesses work six days a week. Payment terms, delivery estimates and legal deadlines are often expressed as “within 30 days”. Enter a number of days in “Add / subtract days” to see the resulting date and weekday. Use a negative number to go backwards, for example to find when a 90-day window started.
